title: Tree diameter → its endpoints
label: ag-multi
statement: A tree has `n` nodes `0..n-1` and `n − 1` undirected edges. Return its **diameter**: the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes.
provenance: "Special diameter endpoints" in an Agoda OA (Nov 2025, FastPrep); "Find Diameter Endpoints of a Tree" scores 82.4% on CodeJeet. Stage 1 is the diameter itself; stage 2 the endpoints, in my words.

stages.title: The diameter
stages.say: Return the length of the longest path in this tree.
stages.require: Implement `TreeDiameter.Diameter(n, edges)`. A wrong edge count → `ArgumentException`.
testNames: starting BFS at 0 is not at an end

stages.title: Every diameter endpoint
stages.say: Several paths may share the maximum length. Mark every node that is an endpoint of some longest path.
stages.require: Add `TreeDiameter.Endpoints(n, edges)`: a string with `'1'` for each such node, `'0'` otherwise.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe two BFS passes find a diameter: the farthest node from anywhere is one end, and the farthest from it is the other; a third BFS from that end gives every node's eccentricity, and a node is a diameter endpoint exactly when its eccentricity equals the diameter. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: A tree has `n` nodes `0..n-1` and `n − 1` undirected edges. Return its **diameter**: the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Is the input guaranteed to be a tree? (Yes; reject a wrong edge count.)
- Diameter in edges or nodes? (Edges.)
- How large is n? (Up to 2×10^5 — no recursion.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: The node farthest from any start is always an end of some diameter — that is why two BFS passes suffice. For the endpoints, a node's farthest distance is always to one of the two diameter ends, so a third BFS gives every node's eccentricity at once.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "T."wo BFS passes find a diameter: the farthest node from anywhere is one end, and the farthest from it is the other; a third BFS from that end gives every node's eccentricity, and a node is a diameter endpoint exactly when its eccentricity equals the diameter."

learn.title: 5 · Why the approach works

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Recursive DFS on a 200,000-node path — stack overflow.
- Trying all pairs (O(n²)).
- Reporting only the two ends found, when other nodes are also diameter endpoints.
- Counting nodes instead of edges.
